summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a mechanical fall from a wheelchair that resulted in a right femoral neck fracture. He underwent closed reduction percutaneous pinning of the fracture and was managed postoperatively with pain control, transfusion of three units of packed red blood cells for anemia, and DVT prophylaxis with Lovenox. His transplant medications were adjusted due to pancytopenia, with Prograf discontinued and Tacrolimus initiated at therapeutic levels. His chronic conditions, including liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and diarrhea, were monitored and remained stable. CMV viral load was undetectable, and a contaminated urine culture for Pseudomonas was disregarded. His appetite improved, avoiding the need for a PEG tube. He progressed well in physical therapy with touch-down weight bearing and was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with a stable hemoglobin, controlled pain, and a comprehensive medication and follow-up plan.
problems: Other closed transcervical fracture of neck of femur
